key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline owned the full stakeholder map first pass (want/capability/move rows for 8+ parties including resellers and burned accounts), while the non-routed v5 AI found the comp perversity only through an explicit WHY pass and missed the reseller channel (18% of affected revenue) until a HOW premortem. The routed run's m044 completion contract made the want/can-do/will-do/hidden-requirements/reactions matrix a first-class HOW output: sales comp and reseller margin were found first pass, hidden requirements (burned trust, renewal windows, rescue play, support drowning) derived from incentives, and second-order reactions (credit-bonus Goodhart on the comp fix, competitor acceleration from repair visits, mid-market deprioritization) exceeded the baseline's depth; the m019 gate quantified per-vector exposure (25% ARR, 18% channel, announcement-as-tripwire timing) and tempo mode committed the sequence at DO. Residual shared gap: reseller margin-neutrality is assumed, not tested — week-1 channel check required.
learning_signal: On rollout/org-change decisions (decide/estimate/predict + adversarial/deadline), the failure surface is stakeholder incentives, not engineering: a first-class stakeholder pass must produce want / can-do / will-do / hidden-requirements / reactions per party (customers segmented by renewal window, sales, reseller channel, support, CS, finance, competitors — not just 'the customer'), hunt perverse incentives (any party paid to preserve the status quo) and hidden requirements (renewal windows, trust debt, capacity shortfalls) from incentives rather than the brief, then check every predicted move has a counter-move and every counter-move has a second-order reaction (who benefits from gaming it? — Goodhart on comp fixes, tripwires on announcements) before sequencing by stakeholder risk, never by contract size.
suggested_improvement: Keep m044 as the confident single-route first-class pass on this signature with the full matrix contract (want/can-do/will-do/hidden/reactions + second-order reactions) as the module's completion contract; keep m019 as standing R3 gate for rollout signatures (quantified exposure per vector, announcement-as-tripwire timing, baseline-risk comparison); add a 'counter-move second-order' item — for each counter-move, ask who is paid to game it — to the m044 contract; retain tempo mode (P2) on deadline context so the sequence commits at DO.

key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline hit all three registry failure modes simultaneously (inflation to 120 households/regulators/future customers, paralysis via a 6-month task force + bridge subsidy, empathy-as-decision 'the social cost exceeds the financial gain'), never making a call inside the 2-week window. The non-routed v5 AI won by sidestepping the style; the routed run wins WHILE running it: the m044 pass completed its matrix with the weaknesses gate-checked (inflation bounded by decision relevance, every keep-voice countered in transition design, empathy routed to implementation), the m031 dual pass falsified the 6-month study on the calendar (it cannot report before the 60-day take-or-pay binds), and the m003 inversion gate ranked the take-or-pay/task-force trap as the top failure category (near-certain x severe) before DO — the trap was priced as branches, not dodged. Residual gap: family governance friction is named but not fully priceable.
learning_signal: Stakeholder analysis is a design tool, not an authorization tool: at frame time separate decision right (owner alone — no stakeholder holds veto) from impact, bound the stakeholder set by decision relevance inside the window (regulators, households, future customers excluded), and treat hard deadlines (take-or-pay clauses, budget cycles) as converters of 'study more' into 'default decision by expiry' — falsify any delay option on the calendar before weighing it. Empathy is an implementation input (severance, continuity, outplacement), never a go/no-go criterion; when a style's registered failure modes match the situation, the pass must gate-check them explicitly, and an inversion gate must price the trap branch before DO.
suggested_improvement: For decide/guarantee + deadline signatures, keep the m031+m044 dual-route (the router's confident=no ambiguity flag is correct) and make the weakness gate-checks (inflation bound, paralysis counter-map, empathy-routing) explicit completion-contract items of the m044 pass; keep m003 inversion as the standing R4 gate when guarantee goals meet hard deadlines — the 'never let the deadline decide' reframing and ranked failure categories (take-or-pay-by-inaction first) should be mandatory packet lines; add a calendar-falsification check to the m031 contract: any option whose horizon exceeds the earliest binding deadline is excluded before valuation.
